A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETAPP research work. All 35 pages, including equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C, support comparison. Full text and rendered-page comparisons identify differences only in the first-page version stamp and Table 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, preference-setting and fine-tuning experiments in Tables 1–3, and comparisons of human and LLM evaluations in Section 4.4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and human–LLM evaluation analyses, with revised numerical results for two models in Table 1.

M1.justification: The ETAPP sandbox, preference and memory framework, tool-invoking procedures, and key-point-based evaluator are unchanged, including the appendix prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 800 cases constructed from 50 instructions and 16 user profiles, with identical tool categories and Tool-Given/Tool-Retrieval scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains identical FC and ReAct comparator rosters. The strategy and fine-tuning comparisons in Section 4.3 also retain the same comparison methods.

E3.justification: The evaluation settings, metrics, 100-case reasoning-model subset, fine-tuning setup and 96-case human-evaluation comparison are unchanged. No protocol revision is documented for the changed Table 1 scores.

E4.justification: The tool-invoking, preference-setting, fine-tuning and evaluator-validation analyses are identical. Appendix B.4 retains the same error examples, and Appendix C retains the same supplementary agreement analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the Bland-Altman analyses and 95% limits of agreement in Section 4.4 and Appendix C. No additional uncertainty reporting accompanies the revised Table 1 values.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises two FC rows: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct's average changes from 0.91 to 1.24, and watt-tool-70B's from 1.08 to 1.11, reversing their average ranking under unchanged reported settings. Several component scores also change, including Llama's Tool-Given PRC from 1.63 to 2.31. All other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The inference and evaluation formulations in Equations 1–2 and the mathematical definitions are unchanged. No derivations, assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about the benchmark, personalization and proactivity, evaluator reliability, and the importance of reasoning.

C2.justification: The interpretations of model performance and evaluator behavior are unchanged. The limitations concerning multimodal tasks and preferences between tools with similar functionality are also identical.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain identical construction instructions, prompts, model identifiers, LoRA hyperparameters and hardware information. Code, model and data-source links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and positioning relative to personalization and tool-augmented LLM research are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 2 March 2025, to v2, dated 12 April 2025. Body wording, headings and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, placement and page layout are unchanged throughout both PDFs. Table 1 changes only numerical entries, which are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: The only scientific revisions are two Table 1 result rows, which reverse the Llama–watt average ranking. Neither PDF explains why the scores changed or establishes that the revised values are more reliable. With methods, validation and discussion otherwise identical, the evidence does not establish whether these revisions improve or diminish overall quality.
